taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America accept Ludwigia repens J.R.Forst.; the later Ludwigia repens Sw. is a different illegitimate homonym.
look_here_first: Inspect opposite paired leaves along a creeping, node-rooting stem. Look for very small yellow petals (when present), but note they may be shed or naturally absent. Crucially, a mature capsule lacks the four dark-green longitudinal bands seen on L. palustris. Do not force submerged sterile specimens to species.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — a peer-reviewed San Marcos River aquatic-plant survey lists Ludwigia repens as native; Joey's Hays County source video independently shows it in the river. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Onagraceae index includes an herbarium specimen of L. repens. Williamson — UT PRC Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: The Hays decision uses a native-status river survey rather than inferring nativity from aquarium occurrence.

best_field_traits: opposite paired leaves on creeping wetland stems, shared with palustris
tiny usually yellow four-petaled axillary flower, but petals may be absent
mature 4-angled capsule LACKS the four longitudinal dark-green bands of palustris
same vegetative architecture as palustris; use mature fruit confirmation when petals absent
morphology_keys.habit: Aquatic perennial, creeping to ascending, sometimes submerged, forming loose mats with adventitious roots at nodes.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Shiny elliptic to obovate or lance-elliptic leaves, often short-petioled but with variable petiole length; blades commonly 0.8–4.5 cm long (FNA).
morphology_keys.flower: Tiny axillary flowers usually with four small pale-yellow/yellow petals and four stamens. Petals are caducous and sometimes absent; the absence of petals alone does NOT establish L. palustris.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey's San Marcos River sequence shows the submerged/creeping form in situ, a useful contrast with the erect shoreline habit of Ludwigia octovalvis.
morphology_keys.stem: Mostly cylindric, often reddish, little or no hair; may root where creeping stem touches moist sediment.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Opposite, usually decussate pairs at each node; primary distinction from alternate-leaved Ludwigia octovalvis.
morphology_keys.ovary: Short inferior green ovary, about 1.5 mm in local specimens, strongly four-angled and roughly funnel-shaped; beneath tiny sepals, often hard to see without macro.
morphology_keys.fruit: Mature capsule often 4–10 mm long (FNA; local Williamson account may be narrower), 4-angled, without longitudinal green bands on the four faces. Contrast L. palustris shorter often 2–5 mm green-banded capsule; sizes overlap.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Repens usually bears small yellow petals but may shed or lack them, whereas palustris normally lacks them. Repens capsule LACKS longitudinal dark green bands; palustris has four dark green capsule bands. Both creep and have opposite leaves; sterile specimens may be unresolved. Hygrophila polysperma is another aquatic look-alike.

diagnostic_image_needs: Real macro of repens mature capsule side showing ABSENCE of four green bands, preferably measured and with direct comparison to palustris ripe fruit.
Sharp exact-species adventitious root emerging from a real creeping repens stem node (1972 drawing in gallery is not a live photo).
Existing Kevin Thiele tiny yellow flower macro now has an accurately placed genus-level arrow; petals can sometimes be absent.

diagnostic_comparison.look_first: Opposite paired leaves along creeping branches vs octovalvis alternate leaves on upright branched stems.
diagnostic_comparison.strong_reproductive_split: Repens four stamens and ca. 6 mm diameter flower vs octovalvis typically eight stamens and 23–39 mm diameter flower in UT PRC specimens.
diagnostic_comparison.strong_fruit_split: Repens bell-shaped capsule locally only 6–7.5 mm long vs octovalvis elongated 38–45 mm capsule.
diagnostic_comparison.caution: Submerged opposite-leaved Hygrophila can mimic this species; without a flower or fruit, use genus-level or unresolved ID when uncertain.

repens_palustris_field_caution: Absence of petals is NOT proof of palustris. Repens petals often shed quickly and may sometimes be absent. If no petals, use mature capsule wall: repens lacks palustris four dark green longitudinal capsule bands.
